Chase Partners With PayPoint to Offer New Cash Deposit Service for Customers
summary:
Chase today announces a new partnership with PayPoint that will enable customers to pay cash directly into their Chase current account at more than 30,000 PayPoint locations across the UK.
The new service gives Chase customers more choice in how they manage their money, combining the convenience of digital banking with the ability to deposit notes and coins locally.
It reflects the continued importance of access to cash services in the UK, giving customers a convenient way to pay cash into their account in communities across the country.
More than 99% of the UK population lives within one mile of a PayPoint store, with some locations open until midnight. 
To make a deposit, customers simply select ‘Pay in’ within the Chase app, choose the current account they want to pay into and enter the amount they want to deposit. The app then generates a barcode, valid for 20 minutes, which can be scanned by the cashier at a PayPoint location before the customer hands over their cash. Customers receive a receipt and the money will appear in their Chase account within 10 minutes.
Customers can deposit both notes and coins, with a minimum deposit of £10. They can deposit up to £500 each month, subject to an annual limit of £6,000, with no fee for using the service.
 
Paridhi Rathore, Head of Payments for Chase, said: “We want banking with Chase to fit around customers’ lives, giving them simple and convenient ways to manage their money.
“Our partnership with PayPoint gives customers the best of both worlds: the ease of managing their money through the Chase app, with the option to deposit cash locally when they need to.”
Anthony Sappor, Banking and Digital Engagement Director at PayPoint, said:
“With more than 30,000 PayPoint locations nationwide, we're proud to provide Chase customers with a simple, convenient way to deposit cash locally and securely whenever they need to.”
By combining Chase's digital banking experience with PayPoint's nationwide retail network, we're making it easier for customers to access essential banking services in the communities where they live and work.

Vivox AI and beSirius Partner to Combine Supplier Assurance and Financial Crime Compliance for Metals and Mining Supply Chains
summary:
Vivox AI, a provider of explainable AI agents for financial crime compliance, and beSirius, which develops AI for assurance and certification readiness in metals and minerals, today announced a partnership. The companies will bring supplier evidence assessments alongside financial crime checks, helping industrial businesses reduce the time and cost of reviewing suppliers and counterparties.
Mining companies, traders and manufacturers routinely ask suppliers for evidence about their operations. Compliance teams also need to understand who owns those suppliers and whether they are exposed to sanctions or other financial crime risks. These reviews often happen separately. The same information gets requested again, while staff spend time searching through records and following up on unanswered questions.
beSirius AI assesses existing operational and supplier evidence against industry standards and company requirements, identifying gaps and producing source-linked assessments. It supports certification readiness, supplier assessments and continuous assurance, helping companies track corrective actions and address critical risks across operations. Reusing evidence across assessments reduces manual work, saving time and money.
Vivox AI brings specialist financial crime screening to supplier and counterparty reviews. Its explainable AI agents examine sanctions alerts and adverse media, investigate complex ownership structures and help identify the people who ultimately control a business. They draw on corporate records and other sources, keeping an audit trail of the information behind each finding. Vivox AI also helps compliance teams work through potential false positives, cutting time spent on manual research and alert reviews.
The partnership is designed to let teams consider these findings together when reviewing a supplier. beSirius shows which claims have supporting documents and what still needs checking. Vivox AI shows whether the supplier's ownership or screening results call for further investigation. The responsible teams review both before making a decision.
The partnership is relevant to companies across the metals and minerals value chain, from mining and refining to trading and manufacturing. beSirius works with Fortune 500 companies in these sectors.
“The beSirius and Vivox AI integration has strengthened our responsible minerals and metals sourcing efforts, enabling us to reduce the time and manual effort required to gather and assess relevant information, including sustainability policies and management systems, ownership information, sanctions screening, and allegations. By bringing this information together in one place, the integration provides us a more efficient tool to support informed sourcing decisions,” said the sustainability team at a Fortune 500 company.
“Investigating a company's ownership can take considerable time, especially when several entities and jurisdictions are involved,” said Tim Khamzin, founder and CEO of Vivox AI. “Our agents help compliance teams work through that information and check the sources behind the findings. Working with beSirius means those checks can be considered alongside the evidence companies already review when assessing suppliers.”
“Companies often have the documents they need, but finding them and checking them against another set of requirements takes time and money,” said Sergey Tyan, founder and chief commercial officer of beSirius. “beSirius uses that existing evidence to prepare assessments that teams can review. Vivox AI brings financial crime expertise to the same supplier questions, including ownership and sanctions risk.”
For Vivox AI, the partnership brings its experience in financial crime checks for regulated businesses into industrial supply chains. beSirius contributes its work with assurance requirements and evidence across the metals and minerals sector. Their findings address different parts of a supplier review.
The aim is to make those reviews less costly and time-consuming. Companies can reuse evidence rather than collecting the same documents repeatedly, while Vivox AI handles parts of the screening research that would otherwise be done manually. Procurement and compliance teams still review the findings and decide which questions need follow-up.

The collaboration integrates beSirius's AI-driven operational and supplier evidence assessments with Vivox AI's specialist financial crime screening, sanctions alerts, and ownership structure investigations. This joint approach aims to help industrial businesses significantly reduce manual work, time, and costs associated with reviewing suppliers and counterparties.
